purpose: Delafloxacin is an antibiotic used to treat certain serious bacterial infections, including skin and skin structure infections like wounds or abscesses. It can also be used to treat pneumonia that was caught outside of a hospital setting. Your doctor prescribed it because it is effective against the specific type of bacteria causing your infection.
how_it_works: This medicine works by attacking the bacteria's ability to copy and repair its own DNA, which bacteria need to survive and multiply. Think of it like jamming the photocopier that bacteria use to make more of themselves. Without being able to reproduce, the bacteria die off and your infection clears up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, headache, and elevated liver enzymes in your blood tests. You might also experience vomiting or a reaction at the injection site if you receive the IV form. Most of these are mild and go away on their own.
warnings: This medication carries an important warning about a small risk of tendon damage, including tendon rupture, especially in patients over 60 or those on steroid medications — stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you feel tendon pain or swelling. It may also cause nerve damage (tingling, numbness), mood changes, or low blood sugar. Avoid taking it with antacids or supplements containing magnesium, aluminum, or calcium, as these can prevent the medicine from being absorbed properly. Tell your doctor if you have a history of seizures or heart rhythm problems.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 450 mg taken by mouth twice daily with or without food, or 300 mg given through an IV twice daily in a hospital or clinic setting. Treatment typically lasts 5 to 14 days depending on your infection. Try to take your doses about 12 hours apart and finish the full course even if you start feeling better.
